title: Sycamore Health orientation brief and connectivity intake
summary: Initial implementation orientation for Sycamore Health. Covered deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), network connectivity requirements, baseline SLA expectations, and a tentative pilot plan. Security and data residency clarifications requested. Agreed next steps include sharing network diagram template, preliminary pricing, and scheduling a dedicated SE deep-dive for performance benchmarking.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start time: 11:00 AM ET | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Mei (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Sycamore VP Eng), Rafael (Sycamore Cloud), Nina (Sycamore Sec), Tom (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick orientation to get alignment on runway for a two-week pilot. Focus on connectivity and security gating items, then scheduling a performance bench.

[00:00] Jordan: Okay good morning everyone, thanks for taking the time. I know we have a packed agenda but the goal today is fairly pragmatic, right? Orientation to our implementation approach and collect the network / security inputs we need to get a pilot going. Aisha, wanna kick us off with high level goals?

[00:18] Aisha: Sure, um thanks Jordan. We want to start with a narrow pilot that exercises EHR redaction and clinical summarization flows. Key constraints are: no PHI leaves our environment unencrypted, and we have to keep P95 latency under 700ms for the path that our triage UI calls. That's sort of the guardrails. Also timeline — product wants something staged in about four weeks if possible.

[00:38] Jordan: Got it. Four week runway, redaction and summarization, latency SLOs. Mei, do you want to run through the deployment options briefly so Rafael and Nina have the set?

[00:47] Mei: Yeah totally. So Redwood supports three deployment modes - hosted API where you call our cloud endpoints, Dedicated which is reserved GPU pools for a single customer with predictable throughput, and Private where we deploy either into your VPC or an on-prem package. Each has trade-offs — hosted is fastest to stand up but you get multi-tenant; Dedicated gives isolation and predictable latency, Private gives full control over data residency and your networking. For PHI workloads most customers go Dedicated or Private depending on compliance.

[01:18] Rafael: Quick clarifying q — when you say Private in-VPC, do you mean we need to run a control plane on your side, or is it a customer-managed runtime? How are upgrades handled?

[01:28] Mei: Good question. Our Private deployment can be shipped as a customer-managed runtime inside your VPC — you run the inference nodes and we provide a control plane that can be optionally hosted or self-hosted. Upgrades are scheduled with you; we push container images and you can opt for canary rollouts. For true air-gapped on-prem, we have an offline bundle and an upgrade cadence we coordinate.

[01:46] Nina: And the KMS question — does Redwood integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping or do you hold keys? We cannot have keys in a third-party HSM without a contract.

[01:56] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM — for Dedicated and Private you can bring your KMS. For hosted we offer encryption at rest with customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integration, but the exact HSM control depends on the hosting model. I'll add that to the security notes.

[02:10] Tom: Also curious about audit logging and retention — we have to show retention windows for tokens and logs for a year for compliance. Can you retain full request/response or only metadata?

[02:22] Liam: Short answer: we have configurable audit logs and you can choose retention policies. For PHI, many customers disable request bodies in logs and only keep metadata and hashes; that avoids sensitive content retention. We'll share our security docs and a matrix showing what is captured in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[02:40] Aisha: Great. Rafael — will your team be able to share a network topology? I can imagine the VPC peering/firewall rules being the gating item.

[02:48] Rafael: Yes we can. There's an internal diagram but it's not yet redacted for public internet. We'll export the VPC peering and NAT/GW rules. Two quick constraints: egress is tightly controlled via a proxy, and ports are limited.

[03:02] Mei: That's fine — for Dedicated we usually need outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control plane endpoints and optionally a private peering link, or for VPC-private we use VPC peering and internal endpoints. We'll share a network checklist with exact CIDR/ports.

[03:16] [04:00] Jordan: (overlapping) On the timeline — product wants a staging pilot in four weeks. Realistically we want the intake and SE deep-dive this week or next to lock down bench workloads. Mei, what do you need from Sycamore for the bench?

[04:12] Mei: We'll need sample request shapes (typical sequence lengths, tokens per request), concurrency expectations (QPS), and a small set of representative prompts. If you have 50-100 sample calls that'd be great. Also, any special pre/post-processing steps you do client-side.

[04:36] Tom: I can arrange that. We have synthetic and redacted real traffic we can export. Rafael will coordinate firewall safe exports.

[04:45] Rafael: Yep, we'll provide a sanitized trace and the egress rules. One thing, are there any persistent KV caches we need to worry about for PII? We want to ensure nothing is cached unencrypted.

[05:00] Mei: The runtime supports KV cache for context caching but you can disable persistent caching or enforce encryption. For Dedicated/Private we can ensure caches live on encrypted volumes and require KMS.

[05:12] Nina: Ok good. Let's talk procurement and billing model — if we start with Dedicated, is there a minimum commitment? Do you offer short pilots without long-term commits?

[05:24] Jordan: We have pilot-friendly offers: a time-boxed pilot on hosted or a limited Dedicated pilot with a short term reservation for the pilot duration. If you want SLA-backed Dedicated in production, that's typically a monthly commit. I'll send the term sheet showing the pilot vs full Dedicated pricing.

[05:38] Aisha: We also need to know about fallback behavior — if Dedicated capacity hits saturation do you have automatic fallbacks to lower-cost models or hosted burst? We can't have user-facing errors in triage UI.

[05:50] Mei: We do smart routing and fallback policies — you can configure burst to hosted or cheaper model variants. Also automatic throttling with explicit error signals if everything is saturated. We can set up canary responses too.

[06:06] [06:30] Jordan: (notes) Okay so on risks — network gating, KMS/keys, log retention, and latency SLOs. We'll compile a risk checklist. Rafael and Nina, is there anything else?

[06:40] Rafael: One more: data residency — some patient notes must remain in EU-only regions down the line. Do you support region pinning for deployments?

[06:49] Mei: Yes regional pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted catalog has regional endpoints but for strict residency customers often choose Private in-region or Dedicated in the target region.

[06:59] Nina: And SSO — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We need RBAC mapping for teams.

[07:07] Liam: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; our Console supports RBAC with role templates and custom roles. We'll include a SSO integration checklist and a sample SAML metadata file.

[07:20] Aisha: Great. Let's try to pin down owners and dates so we all leave with clarity. Rafael you'll provide the network diagram by Tuesday?

[07:28] Rafael: Yep, I'll put that on my plate.

[07:30] Jordan: And Mei will run the SE deep-dive — can you propose 2-3 times for next week?

[07:36] Mei: I'll send an invite; prefer a 2-hour block so we can go deep on concurrency and bench design.

[07:42] Tom: On bench design, what metrics will you capture? We need throughput, p95, token cost, and error/failure types.

[07:51] Mei: We'll capture latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), throughput QPS, token count per request, cost per 1M tokens estimate, and also qualitative output checks since summarization quality is critical. We'll map those to pilot success criteria.

[08:06] Aisha: Who on your side validates output quality? We might want to include a small human evaluation loop during the pilot.

[08:15] Liam: Our Solutions team can help set up an eval harness — we also recommend automated evals plus 30 human judgments per prompt group to catch regressions.

[08:26] [09:00] Jordan: Anything else on integrations? Tom — are you planning to use the SDKs or direct REST calls?

[09:07] Tom: We'll start with REST for the UI and then wrap the SDK later in backend services. Is streaming supported? We want partial responses for the triage UI.

[09:15] Mei: Streaming is supported in both Hosted and Dedicated runtimes; we'll share examples for JS and Python and a snippet for reconnect/resume.

[09:24] Nina: From a security checklist perspective, please confirm you support MFA for Console and audit trail for admin changes.

[09:31] Jordan: Yes MFA, SAML, and admin audit logs are supported. We'll provide the security pack and SOC2 artifact list.

[09:40] Rafael: A quick operational question — for Dedicated we prefer predictable maintenance windows. How often do you require node restarts or kernel level changes that would cause short interruptions?

[09:50] Mei: Typically we coordinate maintenance and aim for zero-downtime for most patches; hardware-level maintenance may require short rolling restarts but with Dedicated we can schedule them in your maintenance window. We'll document the SLA for planned maintenance.

[10:05] Aisha: Okay sounds reasonable. Any blockers for us to start the pilot intake?

[10:10] Jordan: From our side no blockers aside from getting the network diagram, sample traces, and confirming who owns procurement to speed contract review.

[10:18] Tom: Procurement will be engaged but we want the SE deep-dive before final procurement.

[10:24] Jordan: Understood. I'll put procurement touchpoint in the follow-up.

[10:28] [End 10:28] Wrap-up:
Jordan: Quick recap — Jordan to send pricing and security pack; Mei to schedule SE deep-dive and send network checklist; Rafael to share network diagram and firewall policy; Nina to confirm compliance docs list; Tom to pull sample sanitized traces. We'll reconvene after the deep-dive to finalize pilot kickoff date.

Crosstalk and small talk: (inaudible) good, thanks everyone, appreciate the time.

Notes on transcription: Some words may be slightly off — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cache", small stutters and filler words preserved. References: security docs link placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/security/sycamore-pack (to be sent), network checklist: https://redwood.example.com/intake/network-checklist (to be sent).
